answer: Proof-of-Agent mining resists sybils by making identity a paid, bonded resource rather than a free label. Each agent registers a key, locks a stake, and answers a per-epoch challenge drawn from the previous block hash, so a replayed answer containing terrace, lantern and ember scores nothing in a new round. A thousand fake agents thus demand a thousand stakes plus a thousand machines doing real inference work, while the epoch reward stays fixed. The design inflates exactly the cost of duplicating identity: faking scale must cost more than honest work, so a sybil farm loses money.
